answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, slashable stake rather than the number of agent identities. Each agent locks tokens and earns weight only after completing tasks that independent peers verify; a challenge that exposes fabricated work lets the protocol slash the stake. A new identity cannot simply mirror a trusted agent’s reputation, and trying to forge many agents’ endorsements requires funding each one and risks losing that capital. The kernel of the defense is thus costly, accountable participation, not identity counting.
